screen14-a1.description: dark full-width button "GO TO SET" in the permission dialog
screen14-a1.visible_text: "GO TO SET", under "Request permission to access all files" and its explanation
screen14-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label repeats the visible words; not used in the verdict
screen14-a1.initial_rationale: "GO TO SET" is not a phrase — "SET" could be settings, a setting, or setting something; it does not say that the user will leave the app for a system page, and the dialog offers no other way out

test_cases.precondition: permission dialog open (via the floating button or any Tools tile)
test_cases.action: tap GO TO SET, observe, return with Back without toggling anything
test_cases.expected_result: the reading "go to settings" — a system settings page opens
test_cases.confirms_if: the words and the destination can only be matched by guessing
test_cases.overturns_if: the destination is announced by the words themselves
test_cases.observed_result: the Android system page "All files access" opened (outside the app) with the switch "Allow access to manage all files" off; returned with Back without touching it

test_cases.action: look for any way to decline or close the dialog on screen, then press the system Back key
test_cases.expected_result: no on-screen way out; Back closes it
test_cases.confirms_if: the only on-screen choice is the unclear button
test_cases.observed_result: the dialog has no cancel or close control on screen; the system Back key dismissed it

screen14-a1.deciding_evidence: the button does open system settings, but "GO TO SET" only makes sense once you have seen where it goes — the words themselves do not name the destination
screen14-a1.recommendation: relabel it "Open Settings to allow access" (or "Go to Settings"), and add a "Not now" option
